name: Select
description: A native <select> element styled consistently with the Input component. Uses a custom chevron via CSS background-image to replace the browser default arrow. Integrates with FormControl context to receive id, disabled, required, and invalid state automatically.

notes: Uses a native <select> — keyboard navigation and screen reader announcements are handled by the browser/OS.
When used inside a FormControl, the select id is set to the context id so the FormLabel htmlFor links correctly.
aria-describedby is automatically built from '{id}-helper' and/or '{id}-error' when inside a FormControl.
aria-invalid is set when the FormControl is invalid or isError prop is true.
Focus indicator uses a 2px solid outline with var(--color-border-focus) and a 2px offset.
Minimum touch target for md and lg sizes meets the 44x44px requirement.

size.description: Controls the select height, padding, and font size. md and lg meet the 44px minimum touch target.

placeholder.description: Inserts a disabled, empty-value <option> as the first item to act as a placeholder prompt.

multiple.description: Enables multi-select mode. The browser renders a listbox instead of a dropdown.

disabled.description: Disables the select. Also inherited from FormControl context if not explicitly set.

isError.description: Explicitly puts the select into an error visual state. Also triggered when FormControl invalid is true.

children.description: <option> and <optgroup> elements rendered inside the select.

className.description: Additional CSS class names applied to the wrapper div.

sizes.sm: min-block-size 32px — suitable for dense UIs. Does not meet 44px touch target; avoid on touch-primary interfaces.
sizes.lg: min-block-size 48px — for prominent or standalone fields.

do: Always pair with a FormLabel (via FormControl) to provide an accessible name.
Provide a placeholder option for fields where no initial selection should be implied.
Use isError or FormControl invalid prop to signal validation failures.
dont: Do not use for more than ~10 options without considering a searchable combobox instead.
Do not use multiple unless the interface clearly communicates that multi-selection is available.
Do not omit a label — if a visible label is not possible, provide aria-label directly on the Select.
